correctness.rationale: The equilibrium-age identity gives the exact target; rank-by-rank block counting gives the exact leave-a-window-out reward; renewal reward yields the fixed-window bias; and a finite-second-moment regenerative CLT plus an L2-negligible tail reward gives the stated root-n phase. Boundary truncation is controlled by tau_n=o(sqrt(n)).

originality.rationale: Windowed Good-Turing, dependent-sample inconsistency, and duplication models are prior art and are not claimed as new. Searches of the inspected next-token, WingIt, sticky-channel and duplication literature did not locate the exact one-sided renewal-tail bias, its iff fixed-window criterion, or the root-n tail phase. A 2024 random-duplication paper was not inspected in full and remains the principal residual risk.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact dependence quantity controlling one-sided next-token count-surprise bias, produces sharp finite-window and root-n criteria, and yields explicit logarithmic and polynomial window thresholds in geometric and heavy-tailed block models.
